category_title: Students who prioritize narrative storytelling over evidence-based scientific explanation
scenario_title: Oral presentation of creative stories without scientific evidence
minimal_context: The student is giving an oral presentation of a creative story based on the Tricky Tracks activity to the class.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time for your oral presentation. Please share the story you wrote about the Tricky Tracks scenario with the class.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Okay! My story is about an escaped T. rex. It got out and was running around everywhere in the jungle.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay, what happens next in your story?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Well, the T. rex was looking for food and then it found a giant dinosaur egg! ¡Un huevo de dinosaurio gigante! It wanted to eat it, so it started sneaking up on the nest.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Thank you for sharing. Is there anything else you want to add to your presentation?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: No, that's my whole story! The T. rex just takes the egg and runs away into the trees. It was a really great story starter.
